partners.mechanism_chain: GTP cyclohydrolase 1 (HGNC:4153) —DECREASES→ Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) (CHEBI:16978); Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) (CHEBI:16978) —DECREASES→ Nitric oxide synthesis (GO:0004374); Nitric oxide synthesis (GO:0004374) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperphenylalaninemia (HP:0002119); Nitric oxide synthesis (GO:0004374) —LEADS_TO→ Dystonia (HP:0001314). Loss-of-function mutations in GCH1 lead to reduced levels of BH4. BH4 is a crucial cofactor for nitric oxide synthase (NOS). Reduced BH4 impairs nitric oxide synthesis, which is implicated in neurotransmitter regulation and vascular tone, contributing to both hyperphenylalaninemia (due to impaired phenylalanine hydroxylase function, which also requires BH4) and dystonia.

partners.mechanism_chain: PTS (HGNC:9603) —DISRUPTS→ BH4 biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-191856); BH4 biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-191856) —DECREASES→ Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) (CHEBI:17486); Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) (CHEBI:17486) —DECREASES→ Dopamine synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-191858); Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) (CHEBI:17486) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperphenylalaninemia (HP:0002109); SPR (HGNC:10601) —DISRUPTS→ Dopamine synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-191858); Dopamine synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-191858) —DECREASES→ Dopamine (CHEBI:18220); Dopamine (CHEBI:18220) —LEADS_TO→ Dystonia (HP:0001314). Mutations in PTS (Disease A) and SPR (Disease B) both impair the BH4 biosynthesis pathway, leading to reduced levels of BH4. BH4 is a crucial cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) and tyrosine hydroxylase (TH). Reduced BH4 levels in Disease A lead to hyperphenylalaninemia due to impaired PAH activity. In Disease B, reduced BH4 impairs TH activity, leading to decreased dopamine synthesis and subsequent dystonia.

raw.translational: Understanding the distinct yet related molecular underpinnings of these conditions can inform therapeutic strategies. For BH4-deficient hyperphenylalaninemia, cofactor supplementation is a known strategy. For long QT syndrome, therapies often focus on managing cardiac rhythm. Exploring potential downstream effects of BH4 deficiency on cardiac ion channel function, or vice versa, could reveal novel therapeutic targets.

partners.mechanism_chain: PTS (HGNC:9209) —DISRUPTS→ phenylalanine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); phenylalanine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —INCREASES→ phenylalanine (CHEBI:17790); phenylalanine (CHEBI:17790) —LEADS_TO→ hyperphenylalaninemia (HP:0002127); PTS (HGNC:9209) —DISRUPTS→ BH4 (CHEBI:17067); BH4 (CHEBI:17067) —DISRUPTS→ phenylalanine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); CALM3 (HGNC:1487) —DISRUPTS→ potassium channel regulation (GO:0005267); potassium channel regulation (GO:0005267) —LEADS_TO→ QT interval prolongation (HP:0011674); CALM3 (HGNC:1487) —DISRUPTS→ serine/threonine-protein kinase activity (GO:0004674); serine/threonine-protein kinase activity (GO:0004674) —DECREASES→ potassium channel regulation (GO:0005267). Mutations in PTS lead to impaired BH4 synthesis and phenylalanine hydroxylase activity, causing hyperphenylalaninemia. Defective BH4 also impacts downstream pathways.
